marrow__PHYSIO_CH23_Q018.takeaway: Lactate-associated arterial H⁺ sustains ventilation after strenuous exercise.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH23_Q018.displayText: The stimulus to ventilation after strenuous exercise is increased mean arterial H+. Blood lactate raises arterial hydrogen-ion concentration, so respiratory rate remains elevated until the oxygen debt is repaid. Most lactate is converted to glycogen and some is converted to CO₂ and H₂O. This post-exercise acid load, rather than falling arterial oxygen or carbon dioxide, drives the source-keyed response.
emphasis: The stimulus to ventilation after strenuous exercise is increased mean arterial H+

rationales.a: Higher brain-center impulses can contribute to the rapid ventilatory rise at exercise onset, but the question asks the stimulus that persists after strenuous exercise as oxygen debt is repaid.
rationales.c: Arterial PO₂ does not fall as the main post-exercise ventilatory stimulus in this source; elevated H⁺ from lactate is identified.
rationales.d: Decreased PCO₂ would suppress chemoreceptor drive rather than explain the sustained post-exercise ventilation.
